speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me when the rash first appeared and if there is any fever or fussiness?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your age and the rash, did you notice if the skin blisters or if there is pus coming from the lesions? Also, has anyone checked your blood sugar levels recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection (Disseminated Gonococcal Infection presenting as a pustular rash). REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, Gram Stain of skin pustules, and Syphilis serology (VDRL/RPR) for differential exclusion. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin examination photos showing pustules and rash distribution.
